blocks.x: Search for construction companies in Winnipeg, Manitoba and you'll find a long list of results: general contractors, renovation firms and specialty trades. Knowing how to choose a commercial construction company matters, because for a rental building, office or storefront, picking the wrong one can mean delays, cost overruns and liability you didn't expect.
Step 1: Match the company to the project

head: Project
Look for
rows: Renovation contractor that takes on multi-unit work
Commercial renovation contractor with permit and code experience
Specialty trade, or a general contractor who coordinates those trades

blocks.x: A company that's great at new homes may not be the right fit for an occupied apartment building, and vice versa.
Step 2: Check the essentials
Before you request a quote, confirm the items below. Our [contractor checklist](/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-contractor-for-your-renovation-project) shows where to verify each one.

**WCB Manitoba clearance.** WCB Manitoba warns that if you hire a firm that isn't in good standing, you might be liable for its assessment costs. Anyone can pull a clearance letter from WCB's public Clearance Request System, so check before work starts and before each payment.
**Liability insurance.** Ask for a certificate of insurance that names you as the certificate holder, then confirm it with the insurer or broker listed.
**Business registration.** Search the name on the quote in the [Manitoba Companies Office](https://companiesoffice.gov.mb.ca/) registry and check that it matches.

**Permit experience** with the City of Winnipeg for your type of project. The [City's permit search](https://ppdportal.winnipeg.ca/Permits/PropertyPermitSearch/Start.jsp) shows permits issued for a property.
**References** from similar projects, ideally in the last two years.
Step 3: Compare construction quotes properly
The lowest number isn't always the cheapest job. Compare:
**Scope:** does each quote include the same work, materials and finishes?
**Allowances:** what's included vs. left as an allowance that may grow?
**Schedule:** start date, duration, and how they'll work around tenants.
**Payment terms:** reasonable deposits and progress payments tied to completed work, with room for [Manitoba's 7.5% builders' lien holdback](/blog/builders-lien-holdback-manitoba).
**Change orders:** how extra work is priced and approved.
**Warranty** on workmanship.
Step 4: Ask the right questions
Who will be my day-to-day contact on site?
How do you protect occupied units and common areas?
How do you handle surprises like asbestos, hidden damage or code issues?
Will you pull the permits, and who books inspections?
What does cleanup look like at the end of each day?
Red flags
Large cash deposits before any work starts
No written contract or vague scope
Pressure to skip permits
No WCB clearance or certificate of liability insurance
Payment details that change by email
The bottom line
The best construction companies in Winnipeg, Manitoba for your property are the ones that fit your project, answer these questions plainly, and put scope, schedule and price in writing.
